claims.title: Sensor readings may be intercepted between field nodes and the internet-facing gateway
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` remains unverified on `flow:entity:sensor-node>process:device-gateway>publish-readings`, an attacker able to observe the field-network-to-ingest-edge crossing can intercept device-identified sensor readings between `entity:sensor-node` and `process:device-gateway`. The flow crosses a boundary and carries PII; accumulated device identifiers and readings enable correlation of customer-site activity and targeting of individual deployed nodes.

quotes.text: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:sensor-node>process:device-gateway>publish-readings` crosses the field-to-ingest boundary while its transport encryption is unstated, although the attacker must obtain an on-path position. Impact is medium because the flow carries PII-tagged device readings and identifiers that reveal customer-site activity.

mitigations.summary: Verify and require encrypted MQTT transport
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:entity:sensor-node>process:device-gateway>publish-readings` to TLS with broker certificate validation; use mutually authenticated TLS where node capabilities permit.

claims.title: Device registry key material may be intercepted on the gateway lookup path
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:device-gateway>store:device-registry>look-up-device`, an attacker with a foothold on the ingest-edge path can intercept device identifiers, key material, and customer assignments exchanged by `process:device-gateway` and `store:device-registry`. Recovered key material can then be presented to `process:device-gateway` to act as a fleet node, while customer mappings enable targeted follow-on attacks.

quotes.text: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unverified transport because intercepting the intra-edge lookup requires a network foothold. Impact is high because the path handles the shared, unrotated pre-shared credential, and possession enables authentication to the internet-facing gateway.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate the registry lookup
mitigations.detail: Require TLS for `flow:process:device-gateway>store:device-registry>look-up-device` and authenticate the gateway with a narrowly scoped workload identity.
Replace the shared, unrotated fleet pre-shared key with unique device credentials and rotate them, so a captured lookup does not yield fleet-wide standing access.

claims.title: Telemetry records may be intercepted while the normalizer loads BigQuery
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:telemetry-normalizer>store:telemetry-lake>load-readings`, an attacker with access to the analytics-core path can intercept site addresses, occupancy patterns, and readings while `process:telemetry-normalizer` loads `store:telemetry-lake`. The captured records reveal when identified customer premises are occupied and can be correlated with dashboard data later read from the lake.

quotes.text: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the transport posture is unknown and exploitation requires a foothold on the internal analytics path. Impact is high because the confidential telemetry lake contains customer site addresses and occupancy patterns, making captured disclosure sensitive and irreversible.

mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce TLS on `flow:process:telemetry-normalizer>store:telemetry-lake>load-readings`, with authenticated service identities and certificate validation.

claims.title: Fleet dashboard results may be intercepted across the corporate-to-analytics boundary
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:entity:fleet-operator>store:telemetry-lake>query-dashboards`, an attacker observing the corporate-network-to-analytics-core crossing can intercept raw and aggregated customer readings returned to `entity:fleet-operator` from `store:telemetry-lake`. The disclosure includes occupancy patterns and site addresses, enabling surveillance of customer premises beyond the attacker’s own authorized data.

quotes.text: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.
The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the dashboard flow crosses from the corporate network to analytics core and has unverified transport protection, though the attacker needs an on-path position. Impact is high because the flow returns raw and aggregated confidential customer telemetry, including site and occupancy information.

mitigations.detail: Require verified TLS for `flow:entity:fleet-operator>store:telemetry-lake>query-dashboards` and prevent clients from accepting downgraded or unverified connections.
Return only the aggregate and fields required for each operator workflow, reducing the sensitive content exposed on the query path.

claims.title: Gateway-to-Pub/Sub telemetry may be exposed in transit
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:device-gateway>store:pub-sub>forward-readings`, a network observer in the ingest edge can intercept normalized sensor readings written by `process:device-gateway` to `store:pub-sub`. Those PII-tagged messages can be correlated with device identifiers and subsequently with customer assignments obtained from the registry path.

quotes.text: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because both protocol and encryption on the internal forwarding flow are unknown and an attacker needs an ingest-edge network position. Impact is medium because the messages are PII-tagged readings whose correlation can expose customer-site activity.

mitigations.detail: Establish and enforce authenticated TLS for `flow:process:device-gateway>store:pub-sub>forward-readings`; record the actual protocol and certificate-validation posture in the model.

claims.title: Telemetry may be intercepted while the normalizer consumes Pub/Sub messages
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:telemetry-normalizer>store:pub-sub>pick-up-readings`, an attacker observing its analytics-core-to-ingest-edge crossing can intercept PII-tagged normalized readings consumed by `process:telemetry-normalizer` from `store:pub-sub`. The attacker can use the captured stream to reconstruct customer-site activity before it reaches `store:telemetry-lake`.

quotes.text: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and picked up by the telemetry normalizer

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the consumption flow crosses between analytics core and ingest edge while both protocol and transport encryption are unstated, although an on-path position is still required. Impact is medium because the flow carries PII-tagged normalized readings that reveal customer-site activity.

mitigations.detail: Use verified TLS and workload-authenticated subscriptions for `flow:process:telemetry-normalizer>store:pub-sub>pick-up-readings`.

claims.title: A copied device registry could disclose fleet authentication keys
claims.description: `store:device-registry` is confidential, contains credentials, and has unverified `encryption_at_rest`. If that attribute resolves to no effective encryption, an attacker holding a storage-layer copy such as a backup, export, or decommissioned media can read the fleet pre-shared key checks and customer assignments without using the gateway lookup API. Because the credential is shared per fleet and not rotated, recovered material enables later authentication to `process:device-gateway` as deployed nodes.

quotes.text: The key is per fleet, not per device. Nobody has rotated it since deployment.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown at-rest posture: obtaining an operational copy requires storage-layer access, but backups and exports bypass the application path if encryption is ineffective. Impact is high because the confidential registry holds shared, unrotated credential material that can authenticate an attacker to the gateway.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt registry data and operational copies at rest
mitigations.detail: Verify `store:device-registry` encryption and require managed-key encryption for the primary store, backups, exports, and snapshots; restrict export and key-use permissions.
Issue unique device credentials with rotation and revocation so disclosure of one stored verifier or key cannot expose an entire fleet.

claims.title: A copied telemetry lake could disclose customer occupancy patterns
claims.description: `store:telemetry-lake` is confidential and its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If at-rest encryption is ineffective or absent, an attacker obtaining a BigQuery export, backup, or other storage-layer copy can read customer site addresses, occupancy patterns, and readings without authenticating as `entity:fleet-operator`. The disclosure supports persistent surveillance of customer locations and activity.

quotes.text: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because a copied storage artifact is required, but encryption at rest is unverified. Impact is high because the confidential lake contains site addresses and occupancy patterns, whose disclosure enables ongoing surveillance and is irreversible once exported.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the telemetry lake and every export path
mitigations.detail: Verify `store:telemetry-lake` encryption at rest, require managed-key protection for exports, snapshots, and backups, and restrict who can create or read those artifacts.

mitigations.summary: Apply stronger protection to sensitive fields
mitigations.detail: Tokenize or field-encrypt the highest-sensitivity location and occupancy attributes so a copied dataset has less directly usable customer information.

claims.title: A copied Pub/Sub retention artifact could expose telemetry messages
claims.description: `store:pub-sub` holds PII-tagged normalized readings, while both its data classification and `encryption_at_rest` posture are unknown. If retained messages or their operational copies are not effectively encrypted, an attacker holding a storage-layer copy can read telemetry without using `process:telemetry-normalizer` or the normal subscription path. The messages can reveal customer-site activity and may be correlated with records later loaded into `store:telemetry-lake`.

quotes.text: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and picked up by the telemetry normalizer

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the at-rest protection and classification of `store:pub-sub` are unstated, while exploitation requires a retained-message copy. Impact is medium because the store handles PII-tagged normalized readings that can reveal customer-site activity.

mitigations.summary: Establish and enforce Pub/Sub at-rest protection
mitigations.detail: Determine the retention and encryption posture of `store:pub-sub`, require encryption of retained messages and any exports, and limit administrative access to subscription and retention artifacts.

claims.title: Unauthenticated registry access could reveal fleet key material
claims.description: `flow:process:device-gateway>store:device-registry>look-up-device` is a read path carrying device identifiers, key material, and customer assignments, but its authentication is unknown. If the Firestore access path lacks effective caller authentication or an attacker obtains an equivalent access route, the attacker can read registry records from `store:device-registry` rather than merely observe one gateway lookup. Recovered shared, unrotated fleet keys can then be used against `process:device-gateway`.

quotes.text: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because authentication on the registry read path is unknown, so a missing or overly broad storage grant may be exploitable without an internal network foothold. Impact is high because the registry contains credential material that is shared per fleet and not rotated, enabling gateway authentication after recovery.

mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated gateway workload identity for `flow:process:device-gateway>store:device-registry>look-up-device` and deny all unauthenticated or broad interactive reads.

mitigations.summary: Constrain what the lookup can return
mitigations.detail: Expose a verification operation that does not return reusable key material or customer-assignment records beyond what the gateway needs.

claims.title: An unverified Pub/Sub subscription could disclose normalized telemetry
claims.description: `flow:process:telemetry-normalizer>store:pub-sub>pick-up-readings` is a read path for PII-tagged normalized readings, but its authentication is unknown. If subscription authorization is absent or overly broad, an outside attacker can subscribe to or read from `store:pub-sub`, obtaining the same telemetry delivered to `process:telemetry-normalizer`. That stream can reveal customer-site activity and can be correlated with data subsequently loaded into `store:telemetry-lake`.

quotes.text: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and picked up by the telemetry normalizer

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the authentication protecting the Pub/Sub read path is unknown, allowing for the possibility of an accessible or overly broad subscription. Impact is medium because the subscription carries PII-tagged normalized readings that disclose customer-site activity.

mitigations.summary: Restrict telemetry subscriptions to named workloads
mitigations.detail: Require authenticated workload identities and per-subscription ACLs for `flow:process:telemetry-normalizer>store:pub-sub>pick-up-readings`; deny wildcard or anonymous consumers.
Minimize identifiers in Pub/Sub messages and apply short retention limits consistent with the normalizer's processing requirements.
